LESSON: READING 6.2.3 LETTER RECOGNITION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.3 Letter recognition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.3 Letter recognition, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Where can we read letter sounds from? 2. Which letter sounds do you like most? Why?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.3 Letter recognition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Responsibility: Self drive as learner reads and recognize these letters while out of class.

● Unity: Cooperation as learner together with others chant letter sound and letter name rhymes to achieve a common goal of

recognition of the two.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Self-awareness as learner becomes more aware of own abilities in relation to reading and recognizing letter names and letter sounds.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates chanting rhymes for letter recognition to music.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Flash cards,interactive technology, such as educational apps or games designed for letter recognition, letter blocks, flashcards,

posters, charts, interactive games that focus on letter recognition, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as

hearing aids and amplifiers, letter cutouts.
